answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with an aging queue: a new identity pays a small entry fee and waits through a probation window before it can earn or vote, like a lotus that must root before it blooms. During that wait its work is visible but unrewarded, so a single attacker spinning up thousands of accounts faces a ripple of delays and fees that compound faster than any gain, while a lone newcomer crossing one mesa of patience costs almost nothing. Mass creation becomes slow and expensive; honest agents only wait once.
